problems: JARGON — 'LC default', 'cross-default', 'ADNOC Fujairah', 'Vadinar', 'IOCL', 'HMEL', 'MoPNG', 'CCEA', 'MoF', 'RBI ED', 'HPCL', 'Essential Commodities Act directive', 'SBM', 'bbl', 'Paradip', 'Panipat' — a non-oil CEO or PM staffer will lose the thread on the first scan. Every acronym costs 2–3 seconds; the page has 15+ acronyms.

NUMBERS — Performance data uses ranges everywhere: '20–25%', '8–12 days', '5–7 days', '6–13 days below minimum'. Ranges signal the team is uncertain. Pick one defensible number per KPI. Same problem in Decision 2: '600,000 barrels' lands without context — is that 1 day of supply or 30?

BREVITY — Decision 1 alone is 57 words and bundles three separate agencies, three separate asks, and two monetary figures into one sentence. A CEO cannot parse who does what. Decision 2 is 62 words with four separate directives. Both exceed the 5-second rule badly.
ACTION TITLES — The header is strong but the three decision asks have no titles. The CEO sees a wall of text, not three discrete choices. Without titles, priority is invisible.

STORY — The situation paragraph repeats the condensed PS almost verbatim (₹850 crore/day appears in both, ₹2,16,700 crore appears in both, the April 3/5/13 dates appear in both). The second appearance adds no new urgency; it wastes the CEO's 15 seconds of attention budget.

SO-WHAT — Analysis finding 3 ('Standard approval timelines take 5–10 days') ends correctly, but findings 1 and 2 bury the action verb. 'Fixing the banking channel is more urgent than fixing sourcing' describes priority but does not tell the CEO what to sign or by when. So-whats must end with a verb and a deadline.

PYRAMID — Performance data section is a data dump. Four KPIs with variance rows add ~40 seconds of reading. The two most decision-relevant numbers (8-day crude runway, April 13 default date) already appear in the header and situation. The KPI table should collapse to the single number that is not already stated elsewhere, or be cut entirely.

CREDIBILITY — '₹2,16,700 crore in cross-defaults' appears in both the situation and the analysis with no sourcing flag. A number that large with no attribution ('per RBI stress test', 'per IOCL balance sheet') will prompt a CEO to challenge rather than decide.

DECISIONS — Decision 3 mixes a fiscal policy ask (₹30,000 crore transfer + diesel price increase) with an operational ask (crisis decision room). These have different owners, different urgency, and different political risk. Bundling them lets a disagreement on diesel pricing block the crisis room, which is the easier win.

AMBIGUITY — 'Cutting to 70% capacity' in Decision 2 has no cost figure attached. The CEO cannot weigh that trade-off without knowing whether 70% operations saves ₹200 crore or ₹2,000 crore versus the shutdown cost.
fixes: JARGON — First use: spell out every acronym once, then use it. Better: replace agency acronyms with roles in the decision asks. Write 'State oil buyer (IOCL)' once, then 'IOCL'. Replace 'LC default' with 'letter-of-credit default (banks refuse to guarantee crude payments)'. Replace 'cross-default' with 'automatic default on all linked debt'. Cut 'ADNOC Fujairah' to 'the single available UAE cargo'.

NUMBERS — Pick one number per KPI. Recommended: Daily cash burn ₹850 crore (keep — only non-range figure). Secure supply available: use 22% (midpoint, state as 'per IOCL supply desk, April 1'). Bathinda runway: use 8 days (conservative, most decision-relevant). Southern LPG: use 5 days (worst case drives the decision). Add context to 600,000 barrels: '600,000 barrels — 11 days of Bathinda's requirement'.

BREVITY — Split Decision 1 into three one-line sub-asks with owner prefix: 'PMO by April 3 20:00: Grant IOCL Chairman written authority to commit up to ₹15,000 crore per contract without case-by-case sign-off. MoF by April 3 20:00: Backstop IOCL bank guarantees up to ₹60,000 crore. RBI by April 3 20:00: Issue emergency credit headroom to SBI and Bank of Baroda.' Each line is under 5 seconds.

ACTION TITLES — Add a bold one-line title above each decision block. Suggested: Decision 1: 'Unblock payments before April 3 or crude purchases stop.' Decision 2: 'Secure the UAE cargo by April 4 or Bathinda shuts down April 13.' Decision 3: 'Approve fiscal transfer and diesel price increase by April 5 or default is unavoidable.'

STORY — Delete the situation paragraph's second half (everything after 'Both crude supply routes'). That content already lives in the analysis. Replace it with the single fact the situation does not yet state: the political consequence. Suggested addition: 'A shutdown at Bathinda affects 12 million households; southern LPG rationing will be visible to voters within 10 days.'

SO-WHAT — Rewrite Finding 1 so-what: 'Authorize emergency LC headroom to SBI and Bank of Baroda today — before the sourcing decisions in items 2 and 3 become irrelevant.' Rewrite Finding 2 so-what: 'Sign the ADNOC cargo authorization by April 4 08:00 — every other option arrives after the shutdown window closes.'

PYRAMID — Collapse the performance data table to two rows only: the ones not already visible in the header. Keep 'Bathinda crude runway: 8 days' and 'Southern LPG buffer: 5 days'. Delete 'Daily cash burn' (in header) and 'Secure supply available' (the precise percentage is not decision-driving; the consequence already appears in findings). Saves ~20 seconds of reading.

CREDIBILITY — Append a two-word source tag to ₹2,16,700 crore: '(IOCL balance sheet, March 31)'. If that sourcing is unavailable, cut the number and write 'triggers automatic default on the full state-enterprise debt stack' — the CEO's advisor can verify the quantum; the decision does not hinge on the exact figure.

DECISIONS — Split Decision 3 into two asks. Decision 3a (CCEA, political): 'Approve ₹30,000 crore fiscal transfer by April 5.' Decision 3b (MoPNG, operational, lower political risk): 'Stand up crisis decision room with two-hour approval authority by April 4.' This prevents diesel pricing debate from blocking the operational ask, which can be approved faster.

AMBIGUITY — In Decision 2, after 'cut to 70% capacity', add a parenthetical: '(saves ₹X crore in crude consumption, extends runway by Y days — IOCL ops to confirm exact figures before April 4 08:00 meeting)'. If the number is not yet known, flag it explicitly rather than leaving the CEO to assume the trade-off has been quantified.
